title: Create Instacart links only from approved, immutable, idempotent drafts
body:
## Role
A security-minded backend engineer wiring an external call behind an approval boundary.

## Goal
Create the Instacart link through an injected HTTP transport, only for an immutable, approved, unexpired draft, exactly once per idempotency key, and record a truthful attempt.

## Context
Approval envelopes come from #137; the handoff endpoint belongs to the v2 API (#136). Instacart returns only `products_link_url`, documents 400 and 429, and recommends caching a link and regenerating it only when content changes. Shopping-list links have no default expiry, so we set `expires_in` explicitly.

## Deliverables
- `HttpTransport` (production) posting to the configured base URL: development `https://connect.dev.instacart.tools`, production `https://connect.instacart.com`.
- `INSTACART_API_KEY` and `INSTACART_ENV` read from the runtime environment; the key is redacted in `repr`, logs and errors.
- A migration adding `fulfillment_attempts` (draft id, plan version, adapter, idempotency key, status, external link, link expires_at, error code, timestamps, actor).
- The confirm path: verify envelope, then translate (#147), call, store, return.

## Concrete examples
**Primary scenario.** Given approved shopping plan version 7 containing 2 lb carrots, 3 sweet potatoes and a hard "no peanut products" constraint the user has acknowledged, when the Instacart handoff is confirmed, Grocery Butler sends exactly one provider request, stores one expiring fulfillment attempt with status `created`, and returns a "Review in Instacart" link. Repeating the same request returns the same attempt and sends nothing. Modifying the plan invalidates the approval. No order or inventory-received state is recorded.

**Negative cases, each a test:**
- expired approval: rejected, no request
- changed plan version: rejected, no request
- missing `INSTACART_API_KEY`: actionable error, falls back to universal export, no request
- provider timeout or 429: attempt `failed` with a retryable code; a retry with the same key is safe
- unsupported unit or ambiguous mapping: surfaced from #147 before any request
- hard constraint not acknowledged: rejected
- expired provider link: attempt shows `expired`; regenerating needs a new approval for the current version
- duplicate retry: one attempt, one request
- 200 without `products_link_url`: attempt `failed`, never `created`

## Constraints
- No literal key anywhere in code, tests, fixtures, logs, issues or docs.
- Link creation is not order creation; no status implies purchase.
- Errors return stable codes without provider internals or the key.
- The fake transport is the default in tests; a test fails if a real host is contacted.

## Dependencies
#137, #136, #147, #139 (terms allow it), #138 (secret-safe diagnostics).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The primary scenario passes end to end against the fake transport.
- [ ] Every negative case above is a test with the stated outcome.
- [ ] A secret-scanning test asserts the key never appears in logs or error bodies.

## Testing requirements
Fake transport scripted per case; migration tested on SQLite and Postgres; idempotency tested with concurrent confirms.

## Out of scope
UI wording (#149), order or receipt reads, payment.

## Documentation requirements
API contract for the handoff capability; `.env.example` gains commented `INSTACART_API_KEY` and `INSTACART_ENV` with no value; README deployment notes.

## Done-Done (repository requirements)
- Invoke tools through `./scripts/*`, never directly; `./scripts/check-all.sh` exits 0.
- Keep the repository's coverage, typing, lint, security and complexity thresholds; don't weaken any gate.
- No `noqa`, `type: ignore`, disabled checks, test skips or retries added to get green. A flaky test is worse than no test.
- Deterministic contract tests and negative-path tests. Tests use a fake transport; a normal test run never calls Instacart.
- Update the docs and API contracts this change touches in the same PR.
- Review the final diff for Safeway or Instacart coupling in core domain modules (`consolidator`, `pantry_manager`, `recipe_store`, `models`, `pending_actions`).
- The PR body references the epic (#142) and closes this issue.
